answer: A pearl-diving cooperative on a high mesa keeps its ledger honest by asking every newcomer to finish a sequential puzzle chain. The first identity solves 1 chain link, the tenth solves 10 links, and the twentieth solves 20, each link feeding the next so extra computers sit idle. A walnut farmer spinning up fakes faces a wall that grows with every name: 20 fakes demand 210 links in total, each computed in strict order, and buying hardware cannot shorten a chain that only moves forward. Like a single-file trail up the mesa, every extra identity must walk the whole length itself.
